text:
vivian: Quick heads up 1: change window at 11:00 PT today. Deploying api-service v4.0.0 + turning on `ff_autocomplete_precision` in guarded mode. Ramp plan: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 7m observation between steps. We're also enabling the new throttle controller to cap qps per-user to 12 during ramp. Release notes here: https://redwood.internal/releases/v4.0.0. Any blockers?

deploy-bot: Scheduled start: 2024-07-17T11:00:00PT. Canary = 5 instances. Ramp schedule: 5% @t+2m, 25% @t+9m, 60% @t+16m, 100% @t+30m. Auto-pause policy enabled: pause on ERR_RATE_PCT > 0.4 OR error_budget_consumed > 10%/10m. Will post heartbeat.

lee: Adding SLO checks: p95 latency > 180ms for 3m OR sustained cpu throttle > 70% should PAUSE ramp. Also include user-facing error rate (client 4xx/5xx combined).

ana: I'm on docs. Please include the throttle controller command in the runbook. And note: this FF toggles a small deterministic scoring path; expect higher short requests but lower long completion sizes.

pagerduty-bot: On-call rotation: infra-sre is primary. PagerDuty alert policy linked: PD-FF-RAMP. If automation pauses, notify #incidents and runbook owners.

infra-sre: Confirmed. I'll keep tracing and heap metrics open. @deploy-bot, can we get a one-line rollback ink in thread?

deploy-bot: Operator rollback snippet:
```
# rollback FF and restore throttle
redwoodctl ff set ff_autocomplete_precision off --reason "rollback: automated pause"
redwoodctl throttle set api-service qps-per-user 50 --note "restore pre-ramp default"
# pin model routing if needed
redwoodctl routing pin model prod-v1.9 --duration 45m
```

vivian: Added to runbook: if automated pause fires, first step = pause ramp -> collect top10 traces -> notify #incidents -> decision to proceed or rollback within 15m.

lee: One more automation ask: can the ramp pause create a short-lived maintenance flag so UI teams don't misinterpret errors? If so tag @frontend.

deploy-bot: Canary at 5% stable @t+4m. Proceeding to 25% @t+9m.

ana: Watching doc hits. Not seeing significant change in median tokens. Token-cost estimate updated on release doc (+3%).

deploy-bot: Hit 25% @t+10m. Observability note: request amplification metric up ~6%. Monitoring SLOs.

lee: small p95 spike at t+12m to 195ms, but not sustained. No pause.

infra-sre: Heap growth on one canary pod noted but GC recovered. Keeping eye.

deploy-bot: Proceeding to 60% @t+18m. Will hold 7m.

lee: At t+22m automated pause triggered: error_budget_consumed = 12% over 10m. Ramp paused at 60%.

vivian: Good catch. Runbook step: collect traces + top logs and tag @mobile @web. Decide to continue or rollback after 10m investigation.

ana: Docs updated: paused state noted. Sending short announcement to product stakeholders.

infra-sre: After digging, one backend shard hit a degraded network path causing retries. Not related to FF logic. We can proceed once we confirm route fix.

deploy-bot: Operator commands for investigators:
```
redwoodctl ff status ff_autocomplete_precision
redwoodctl infra diagnose shard-7 --since 30m --output brief
```

lee: After fix validation p95 back to baseline at t+30m. Recommend resume to 100% but with slower final step: 60% -> 80% -> 100% with 5m holds. Agree?

vivian: Agree. Proceed with the slower tail. Keep pin on model routing for 45m from now as buffer.

deploy-bot: Resuming ramp: 80% @t+34m -> 100% @t+40m.

infra-sre: Monitoring green. No cache hit degradation.

deploy-bot: Full rollout complete @t+41m. Final checklist: throttle controller remains active for next 2h, model routing pinned to prod-v1.9 until +45m. If any regressions open this thread and tag infra-sre + oncall.

ana: Release notes: v4.0.0 shipped. Added section about automated pause and how to interpret alerts.

vivian: Thanks team. I'll hand this to weekly release notes and archive thread. If anything else crops up, reply here. :rocket:
